subject.title: [Feature Request] SKILL.md Instruction Isolation from Agent Context

question: Should installed skills remain trusted operator-provided instructions governed only by agent/session policy, or should OpenClaw introduce a distinct per-skill runtime principal with enforceable tool and memory capabilities?
rationale: The model cannot enforce its own role lock, and current tool calls are not reliably attributed to an active skill; choosing a new principal and compatibility model changes OpenClaw’s documented trust boundary and existing skill behavior.

options.title: Add a runtime-enforced skill principal
options.body: Design typed skill activation identity and capability enforcement at tool, memory, sandbox, and approval boundaries before implementing prompt-level defenses.

options.title: Keep skills as trusted operator state
options.body: Retain the current trust model, strengthen documentation and scanning, and narrow this issue away from claims of enforceable instruction isolation.

options.title: Start with inspect-only manifests
options.body: Land capability declarations and inspection without enforcement as a staged foundation, while leaving the central isolation gap explicitly unresolved.

recommendation.title: Add a runtime-enforced skill principal
recommendation.body: Design typed skill activation identity and capability enforcement at tool, memory, sandbox, and approval boundaries before implementing prompt-level defenses.
